findings.claim: The new README section and MsgPack004 doc state that diagnostics for metadata-only types are reported by the defining assembly and that the consumer does not analyse them. This is deliberate per the ledger, not a defect. The dropped diagnostics and the lack of a consumer-side formatter for such types match the recorded behaviour.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed and a missing diagnostic or formatter for them is not a defect. The README and MsgPack004 doc text is consistent with it.

findings.claim: The wrapper that drops diagnostics whose location is outside the compilation is installed for every analyzer diagnostic, not just the metadata-symbol paths. Diagnostics with no location (Location.None), where IsInSource is false, still pass through. Diagnostics anchored in another syntax tree are silently suppressed. This broad filter could hide wrong or valid reports, and L10 notes the analyzer has been sensitive to false positives. The tests only cover the unkeyed-member case, not other diagnostics (MsgPack003/005) against the filter.

receipt_plan.detail: Change the filter to always report, or always drop. Run the analyzer tests in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests and check that existing MsgPack003/004/005 tests still fail or pass as expected. A surviving mutant would show the filter is untested.

findings.claim: The new test helper asserts no diagnostics only for the generator run, using LanguageVersion.CSharp7_3 by default for the struct tests. The new docs claim that record structs and generic value types are supported. The record struct test passes the generator test only with Latest. Nothing verifies that the generated resolver content, rather than only its hint name, handles Item<int> correctly. SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck is also set.

receipt_plan.detail: Read RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync: it asserts only that the hint name exists, and SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck skips content verification. Compile the generated output to see whether Item<int> gets a formatter.
